title: Polenta e Salsiccia
subtitle: Soft polenta with Italian pork sausage and red wine
excerpt: Polenta e salsiccia is a northern Italian winter supper: creamy polenta served with a simple sauce of Italian pork sausage browned in red wine with rosemary. The sausage fat enriches the sauce; the polenta soaks it up. It is a dish of the farmhouse kitchens of Lombardy, Veneto, and Emilia.
sourceNotes: Polenta with sausage is a classic of northern Italian domestic cooking. Pork sausage with red wine and rosemary is one of the most common winter meat preparations across Lombardy, Veneto, and Emilia-Romagna.

content.text: The polenta should be started before the sausage sauce, as it takes 40 to 45 minutes. The sausage sauce is quick -- it needs about 20 minutes once the sausages are browned -- so timing the two to finish together is straightforward.

Bring 1.2 litres of water to a boil with {{salt-table}} salt. Pour in {{polenta}} polenta in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Reduce to very low heat and cook for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until thick and pulling away from the pan sides. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{parmesan}} Parmesan.

Heat {{olive-oil}} olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown {{sausages-pork}} sausages all over for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{rosemary}} rosemary and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{red-wine}} red wine and let it bubble. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the sausages are cooked through and the wine has reduced to a sticky sauce.
Serve the polenta in bowls with the sausages and their sauce on top.

items.symptom: The polenta is sticking badly to the pan
items.cause: The heat is too high, or it has not been stirred enough.
items.fix: Polenta must cook at a very low simmer. Use a wide, heavy pan and stir every 3 to 4 minutes. A crust on the bottom is normal and adds flavour; sticking and burning are not.

content.text: Polenta and sausage is the emblematic supper dish of the Italian Alpine farmhouse. It is made across Lombardy, Veneto, Trentino, and Friuli. The sausage is typically Italian-style pork sausage flavoured with fennel seeds and pepper. The combination is filling, warming, and deeply satisfying -- the kind of food that has been eaten in these regions on cold evenings for three centuries.
